newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel little changed against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Shekel little changed against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday after the Bank of Israel intervened, dealers said.

"The dollar was traded slightly lower abroad and this led to a mild rise of the shekel against the U.S. currency. The basket was almost unchanged after the Bank of Israel intervened in trading to raise the basket to seven percent below the diagonal rate," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
"Companies are using the opportunity of the strong dollar to sell them knowing that the central bank has to buy dollars to support the basket," the dealer said.

Currency traders estimated that the central bank bought 320 million shekels in dollars on Monday to support the basket, as the dollar rose to 3.2870 shekels from 3.2700 on Friday. Traders said the extent of intervention today was considerably lower.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2840 shekels against 3.2870 shekels on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6210 shekels against 3.6206 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7871 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7876 on Monday and against the mark at 2.0255 shekels against 2.0206 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2830 shekels.
